title: Line
summary: A line is a straight path of points extending forever in both directions. Explore how lines are drawn, named, and used as the base of segments, rays, and angles.

compareCandidate.label: Line vs. segment
compareCandidate.description: A line extends forever both ways with no ends; a segment is a piece of a line with two clear endpoints.

plainLanguageExplanation: A line is a perfectly straight path that goes on forever in both directions. It is made of an endless string of points, and you show its never-ending ends by drawing small arrowheads. You name a line with two of its points in any order, like line AB or AB. A line has no thickness and no endpoints — it just keeps going. Slice a line to make its cousins: stop both ends for a segment, or stop just one end for a ray.

keyFacts.value: Countless points in a straight row

keyFacts.label: Cousins
keyFacts.value: Stopping the ends makes segments and rays

whyItMatters: Lines are everywhere — roads, edges, laser beams, and horizons. Knowing that a line goes on forever is what lets geometry talk about direction, straightness, and the pieces we cut out of it.
didYouKnow: You can never draw a complete line — it goes on forever in both directions, so every line you have ever seen is actually just a piece of the real one.
compareReason: Students blur lines with segments — comparing shows the infinite ends vs. the two endpoints.
